Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, procurement@aegishealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity kickoff — initial ask and data pull

Hi Sarah / Aegis ops team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Dedicated. To get the dedicated GPU pool provisioned and scoped correctly, we need a short set of inputs from your side — traffic shape, peak TPS for inference, regional preference, and any compliance/network constraints. I attached a quick worksheet (aegis_gpu_requirements.xlsx) and our multipool template for reference.

High level proposal from our side (subject to your numbers):
- Initial base pool: 4x NVIDIA A100 (40GB) in primary region, with optional 2x warm GPUs for burst.
- Autoscale trigger: sustained queue > 60s or CPU/GPU util > 75% for 2 intervals.
- Burst: up to 2x additional A100s for short windows (configured as pre-warmed, billed proportionally).
- Regional fallback: primary us-west, failover eu-west (TBD based on latency numbers).

Please fill the attached sheet and return the Aegis traffic snapshot by EOD tomorrow if possible. Procurement is cc'd for visibility.

Attachments: aegis_gpu_requirements.xlsx (xlsx), redwood_multipool_template_v2.pdf (pdf)

Next steps I propose:
1) Aegis returns traffic snapshot + preferred regions (Sarah).
2) Redwood proposes detailed pool YAML + cost estimate (Ben).
3) Implementation kickoff (Priyom) and netops checklist.

Happy to hop on a quick 30m slot if that accelerates things — propose Wed 10–12 PT.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Provisioning plan & surge policy alignment — AegisHealth

Hi Sarah / team,

Thanks for the snapshot — good detail. Based on the 1,800 QPS peak and monthly 3x spikes, here's our recommended config and autoscale/burst policy:

Proposed pool (per region):
- Base: 6x A100 40GB (sustains steady 1,800 QPS with headroom for model diversity).
- Warm reserve: 2x A100 (keeps KV caches hot for common prefixes).
- Burst ceiling: +6x A100 for rapid expansion (total ceiling 14 GPUs).

Autoscale policy (summary):
- Scale up: sustained token queue >50 requests for 45s OR GPU util > 78% for 2 consecutive 30s intervals.
- Scale down: idle <15% utilization for 2 minutes, with minimum base preserved.
- Cold-start protection: maintain warm reserve for top 3 endpoints; pre-warm model weights during known monthly batch windows (we can schedule warm-ups).
- Billing model: base pool billed monthly; burst billed per-minute on consumed GPUs.

Regional selection: primary US-West (closest to your clients), secondary EU-West for failover — we recommend cross-region routing at the edge with active-active for read-only lower-latency endpoints and active-passive for stateful requests.

Operational notes (implementation):
- KV cache seeding will reduce burst latency by ~30–50% for repeated prompts.
- For the monthly 10–15 minute spikes, enabling scheduled pre-warms on the expected windows reduces cold-start cost.
- If you require preemption safety, we'll set per-request fallbacks to a smaller quantized model variant.

Attached is the YAML skeleton for the pool and a rough cost estimate. Please review and flag any netops/VPN constraints.

Attachments: proposed_pool_config.yaml (yaml)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Looping in implementation notes and netops checklist so we can schedule the kickoff. Summary of next steps and asks from Aegis:

1) Network & IAM
- Confirm VPC CIDR ranges and whether VPC peering or private link is preferred.
- Provide service account email for infra provisioning.
- Netops doc attached: vpc_peering_checklist.md

2) Compliance artifacts
- We can provide SOC2 audit summary, data flow diagrams, and deployment hardening checklist. If you need the full report we will coordinate an NDA request.
- Drafted an SLA exception request (SLA_exception_request_draft.docx) for the monthly burst ceilings — please review.

3) Cutover and timeline
- Provisioning: 3–5 business days after netops details + signed SOW.
- Dry-run: schedule a controlled 15-minute spike window to validate autoscale and KV warm-up.
- Go-live: target two-week runway post dry-run for monitoring and ops playbooks.

4) Regional choices & latency targets
- Recommend primary in us-west-2 (Oregon) and secondary in eu-west-1 (Dublin).
- We can add additional edge routing in us-east for East-coast users if latency tests suggest.

Action items (owners):
- Sarah: confirm VPC peering preference + provide service account (by Tue EOD).
- Procurement: review SOW and return signed copy.
- Irene: schedule kickoff once netops confirms availability.
- Ben/Priyom: finalize pool YAML & cost estimate based on confirmed netops inputs.

Attachments: vpc_peering_checklist.md (md), SLA_exception_request_draft.docx (docx)

Thanks — happy to take a 30m onboarding window next Tue or Wed.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Implementation Lead
Redwood Inference
